summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-10-10. Search tool usage ran out partway through, so the scan was narrower than planned. I found two institutional-blunder candidates, each with two accepted publishers opened and both quotes checked word-for-word against the fetched pages. (1) Athens-Clarke County, GA elections department sent a second absentee ballot to 1,154 voters because the mailing list it gave the printer repeated addresses from an earlier list (CBS News Atlanta, WSB-TV). (2) South Portland, ME is reprinting 19,000 municipal ballots because the printer transposed the bond total, showing about $105.4 million instead of $150.4 million (Press Herald, WGME). Both are institutional blunders with no one harmed, so they fit the rules on official errors, including the line that 'the vendor did it' doesn't excuse the body that hired the vendor. Earlier ballot stories were set aside as clerical errors, though, so the verifier may weigh them the same way. Athens-Clarke ranks first because the faulty list came from the county itself, not a vendor. Genius: Genius scan for 2026-10-10 (window 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-10). This year's Nobel announcements gave two US-based laureates. On Oct 5, Stanford's Karl Deisseroth shared the medicine prize for optogenetics. On Oct 6, UW-Madison's Francis Halzen won the physics prize for the IceCube neutrino observatory. I opened at least two accepted-publisher pages for each and checked the quotes against the fetched text. I hit the search tool's usage limit before I could vet any non-Nobel stories, so only two candidates are submitted. Pair published.

UW-Madison physicist Francis Halzen wins Nobel Prize for detecting high-energy neutrinos from space

Handcuffed suspect hot-wires patrol car window and escapes in Thurston County, Washington

candidates.headline: Wayne County, Michigan, resends at least 8,500 mail ballots after printing error
candidates.reason: Reported Oct. 2, before the 7-day window that starts Oct. 3. Only Votebeat, which is not on the accepted list, was seen.

candidates.headline: Kendall County, Illinois, sends 300 wrong mail-in ballots to two precincts
candidates.reason: Already set aside in a recent scan with no new facts, and the only source found (Shaw Local) is not on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: Oregon state Rep. Paul Evans apologizes after DUII arrest
candidates.reason: Possible addiction issue, and the only pages found were KOIN and Yahoo, neither of which is an accepted source.

candidates.headline: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai win 2026 Nobel Prize in chemistry
candidates.reason: Not in the US: the laureates are based in France and Japan.
